reconcile.connective: Defenders read "ascended" in John 3:13 as ascending to fetch down divine knowledge, not bodily translation, so Enoch and Elijah pose no exception.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells of the Skeptic's Annotated Bible — the upstream source for this row — presses the plain wording: John 3:13 says no one but the Son of Man has ascended, yet Genesis 5:24, Hebrews 11:5, and 2 Kings 2:11 already had Enoch and Elijah taken up.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Though Enoch and Elias had, yet not by their own power, nor in the sense our Lord designs; whose meaning is, that no man had, or could go up to heaven, to bring from thence the knowledge of divine and heavenly things …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: The single note that explicitly names Enoch and Elias, concedes they were taken up, and resolves the tension by restricting John 3:13's "ascended" to ascending-to-fetch-down-divine-knowledge — the exact harmonization of this contradiction. Truncated at a source semicolon, so ends with the elision marker.

pd_work.note: Gill treats this passage directly, conceding Enoch and Elijah were taken up but reading John 3:13's "ascended" as going up to bring down the knowledge of heavenly things; Haley's coverage of this specific pair could not be confirmed, so the row-surfaced harmonizing commentator is used per spec.
